  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Evolution Hockey, "Small Area Game - In-Zone 3 v 3." In-zone 3v3 compete game. Not Ramsay's race-to-the-puck start; same 3v3 in-zone battle.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position

  • Directions: Skill clip on attack position for 1v1s—hands away, hip protection, attack the defender’s heels/hands. Use as a 30-second demo before 1v1 station work.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lexj0b5n7Ks

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Oreo

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOLeLJdgGA
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "3v3 Continuous." Continuous 3v3 game. Not Lammers' Oreo (D must pass to the next players in line).

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)

  • Directions: This is a phenomenal drill in several ways. First, the concept of this drill can be used in many different areas of the ice. Secondly, it forces players to think 2 on 1's in tight spaces.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WXvZcoC_yxA

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Passing support & give-and-go). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull the far-end net to the boards and set two tires on the goal line (tire targets). If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 2: *Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*. The race decides offense; offense attacks Liam. If the defenders win the puck they score by carrying it through a cone gate at the tops of the circles. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets). Cross-ice; one team shoots on Liam, the other scores by hitting 2 tires at the far end; flip ends every time the tire team scores. Tonight's constraint: a goal on Liam or a tire counts only after a completed give-and-go. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Oreo*? Keep it on Liam's net (offense scores, defense outlets to the next line); cap shifts at 30 s so the shot count stays sane.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Gates Passing Small Area Game (partners); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)* → Attack only toward Liam's net; when the backcheckers win the puck they 'score' by passing to their partners waiting in the small neutral zone. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 v 2 Dot Jumper. 2v2 race on a coach chip; each team's dot player is frozen until it gets a pass, then jumps in for a 3v2 on Liam's net. Theme rule: the dot player must return the puck (give-and-go) before anyone shoots. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)* → Cross-ice with Liam in one net; the other net is replaced by two tires — a 'goal' there is hitting a tire after a pass. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only off a pass (catch-and-shoot or give-and-go); no rebound pile-ons after the whistle.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey). USA Hockey: warm the goalie first, quality over quantity, and let him hop out for a few reps in high-volume drills.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2jPl1Ind8E0
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hockey Backcheck - Backchecking against a 2 on 1 and 3 on 2." Official IHS backcheck / tracking clip. Not Perry Pearn's 45-degree tracking game; run the written tracking-game rules.

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Ramsay 3 V 3 Race

  • Directions: Jason Lammers describes the Ramsay 3 V 3 Race. This competitive small area game incorporates racing to the puck to determine which team is on offense. Setup Full ice setup with goalies in both nets.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2I8V86FKg10
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Evolution Hockey, "Small Area Game - In-Zone 3 v 3." In-zone 3v3 compete game. Not Ramsay's race-to-the-puck start; same 3v3 in-zone battle.

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Directions: Warm-up flow that links retrievals to first-pass exits. Skaters retrieve, hit a support target, and transition up ice without standing still. Great for D breakout habits.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *NZ Give and Go* — already goalie-free; run as written.

  • *Contact sprinkle (Perry Pearn Tracking Game)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean). Below the circles, 3 F vs 2 D + Liam; F goal = 1, D skate it past the line = 1, Liam freeze = 1; first to 5. Tonight's constraint: D/goalie point only counts if Liam set the puck or the D made a first pass to break it out. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*? The race decides offense; offense attacks Liam. If the defenders win the puck they score by carrying it through a cone gate at the tops of the circles.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Neutral Zone Passing Station #1; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* needs no net — run it, then use the remaining minutes for 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game: Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Theme rule: Liam starts every rep by stopping a rim and setting it for the D. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)* → Cross-ice 3v3 to one net: the forecheck team attacks Liam; the retrieving team must skate behind Liam's net and then score by hitting a tire at the far end. The F1 pressure rule stays. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Count Liam's rim stops and puck-sets as reps; shots only at the end of an entry, never rapid-fire.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!

  • Directions: Open practice with a 12-player SAG so everyone is active immediately. Use a half-zone or below-dots box, short shifts, and a simple scoring rule. Sets tempo and compete early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact|skills

Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUwNEdJtFAs
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "NHL Development Camp Race to Puck Game." Official IHS race-to-puck clip (Sabres camp 1v1 into a 2v1), not Elle Hartje's circle possession game. Same first action: win the puck race.

Station 2 — systems|sag|contact

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk

Station 3 — skills|goalie

Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Offensive-zone timing drill: receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release, weight transfer, and getting the puck through from tough angles. Feed Liam quality looks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Angle Behind Net + Stick Check

  • Directions: O carries behind the net; X angles to force outside/into the corner and finishes with stick lift/press or controlled rub—no open-ice charge. Switch roles every few reps. Cue: stay slightly behind until the carrier clears the net, then close.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

C. Small-area game (28–42)

USA Activation Drill (14U+)

  • Directions: Coach shoots a puck across; first two from each line race to it while the next two become activating D behind the nets. Possession side can attack or kick back to activating D for a 4v2. Run 30-second shifts; teach battle + activate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

3 on 3 Add a D

  • Directions: This small-area game emphasizes encouraging your defense to join the rush while working on quick transitions, support, puck movement, and recognizing when to activate the extra player. Setup Shorten the rink by placing each net at the tops of the circles. Teams line up 3 on 3 in the neutral zone.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=34RNIP3F0Gg
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Sanesports, "Zone Entry - 3v3 +D Joining Rush - 2/3 ice." Same idea (D activating into a 3v3 rush / transition); video is 2/3-ice zone entry, not nets at the tops of the circles. Run the written setup.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (O-zone cycle & low-to-high). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!*: Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Puck Race to Possession Game*) → no-goalie: Gates Passing Small Area Game (partners). Pairs pass through cone gates, can't reuse a gate twice in a row; count gates in 45 s. Keeps tonight's focus (O-zone cycle & low-to-high) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)*) → no-goalie: Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies). Keep-away inside a faceoff circle (2v1 → 3v1 → 4v2 monkey-in-the-middle); no goalie needed. Keeps tonight's focus (O-zone cycle & low-to-high) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Angle Behind Net + Stick Check)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Swiss 4 vs 2 Scoring Game. Zone split high/low into two 2v1s on Liam's net (4 v 2); defenders stay in their area, shot within ~5 s. Tonight's constraint: every goal needs a low-to-high pass first. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *USA Activation Drill (14U+)*? The possession side attacks Liam (or kicks it back to the activating D); if the other side wins it, they score by hitting a tire at the far dot after a D-to-D pass.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Gates Passing Small Area Game (partners); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *3 on 3 Add a D* → Keep Liam's net; replace the other net with two tires. The team going toward the tires must hit its activated D with a pass before it can score on a tire. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net. Below the circle tops, one net; team of 3 must always keep a forward below the goal line, D talk through the switches. Theme rule: the player who comes out from behind the net must cycle up the wall and the next forward rotates down. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp* → One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Low-to-high point shots must be low and tippable; no clappers from the blue line.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Liam's station — Station 3: *New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG*. The winner's exit shot goes on Liam; during his rest windows the exit shot goes at a tire in the empty net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

Side Middle Side

  • Directions: The Side Middle Side passing drill from Darryl Belfry is from his practice plan, Parallel Teaching Structure - Passing Between Two Checks and One Touch Passing . Setup Players line up at all 4 neutral zone face-off circles with pucks.

Station 1 — sag|skills

Ride The Bull

  • Directions: Objective Ride The Bull is a small area game from Matt Thomas that works on developing puck protection and possession skills under pressure. Teams must protect the puck, use their teammates, and keep possession for 8 seconds. If they are able to accomplish this, they are awarded a 3rd teammate and each teams begin game play to try to score on the opposing teams net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-mjFcY9jvJg
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "3 v 2 Puck Protection Game." Official IHS 3v2 puck-protection game (Daniel Paille). Not Ride The Bull's 8-second possession then add a player; same protect-the-puck-under-pressure theme.

Station 2 — contact|sag

New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG

  • Directions: Below-hash or half-zone boxes. Dump a puck; 1v1 then 2v2 with legal contact taught that night. Winner exits to a shot. Stop illegal hits immediately. Angle first, stick second, body third.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04EKvozxnmk

Station 3 — warm-up|skills

Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Bentley Wall Cycling Drill

  • Directions: This drill helps players work on their wall play and cycling under pressure. SETUP: This is a half ice drill, there should be a net in its usual spot on the goal line. There should be a line of players starting on one of the dots with a pile of pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jMDpyps_a3Q
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Half Ice Hockey Drill: Continuous Cycle Drill." Official IHS continuous cycle drill. Not Bentley Wall Cycling; same wall-cycle / cycle-under-pressure work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Special-teams habits (PP entry / PK pressure)). Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Ride The Bull*) → no-goalie: The Gate Game (no goalie). 3v3, score by passing through one of three tire gates to a teammate; no net, no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Special-teams habits (PP entry / PK pressure)) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG*. The winner's exit shot goes on Liam; during his rest windows the exit shot goes at a tire in the empty net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Power Play Scoring Competition (Wes Wolfe). 60-s PP rounds on Liam: 5-on-0 entry, then one PKer added every 15 s up to 5-on-4; most goals wins. Tonight's constraint: entry must use the planned route (drop or kick-out); PK earns a point for every clear. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)*? Attack only toward Liam's net; when the backcheckers win the puck they 'score' by passing to their partners waiting in the small neutral zone.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free The Gate Game (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps. Contact every practice.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — contact|sag

New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG

  • Directions: Below-hash or half-zone boxes. Dump a puck; 1v1 then 2v2 with legal contact taught that night. Winner exits to a shot. Stop illegal hits immediately. Angle first, stick second, body third.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04EKvozxnmk

Station 2 — warm-up|skills

Side Middle Side

  • Directions: The Side Middle Side passing drill from Darryl Belfry is from his practice plan, Parallel Teaching Structure - Passing Between Two Checks and One Touch Passing . This specific drill allows the whole team to warm up their skating, puck handling, passing and vision at the beginning of the practice. Setup Players line up at all 4 neutral zone face-off circles with pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeRHZLK2eek

Station 3 — sag|skills

3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward rule (e.g., clear/score after a takeaway). Offense must move to support; defense angles first, then stick, then body. Continuous short shifts so everyone gets reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Bentley Wall Cycling Drill

  • Directions: This drill helps players work on their wall play and cycling under pressure. SETUP: This is a half ice drill, there should be a net in its usual spot on the goal line. There should be a line of players starting on one of the dots with a pile of pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jMDpyps_a3Q
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Half Ice Hockey Drill: Continuous Cycle Drill." Official IHS continuous cycle drill. Not Bentley Wall Cycling; same wall-cycle / cycle-under-pressure work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game

  • Directions: 3v3 version of Gates of Buffalo. Teams score by completing passes through cone/tire gates while moving to open ice. Progress by shrinking gates or adding a defender.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adueXqyfyNs

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Puck protection under contact). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Liam's station — Station 1: *New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG*. The winner's exit shot goes on Liam; during his rest windows the exit shot goes at a tire in the empty net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 2: *Side Middle Side* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 3 (*3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM*) → no-goalie: Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game. 1v1 in the middle with wall support; carry it across outside the cones = 1 pt, through the middle gate = 2 pts; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Puck protection under contact) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Tonight's constraint: a goal counts double if the scorer protected through contact on the wall first. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward*? Already half-ice to one net — keep it on Liam's net; the defensive reward stays a clear/outlet pass to the coach, so no second net is needed.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Bentley Wall Cycling Drill* → Already a one-net half-ice drill — keep it on Liam's net and alternate sides every rep so shots come from both walls. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Theme rule: the below-goal-line rule forces a protected carry or pass under pressure. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* is goalie-free — run as written; Liam does 2 minutes of easy lateral movement and stretches in the crease.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only after the carrier separates; no hacking at rebounds under his pads.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team

  • Directions: Full-team warm-up with five pucks moving. Players keep circulating, exchanging passes, and filling lanes so the ice stays alive. Great openers for touch, awareness, and tempo before stations.

Station 1 — sag|skills

Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)

  • Directions: This is a phenomenal drill in several ways. First, the concept of this drill can be used in many different areas of the ice. Secondly, it forces players to think 2 on 1's in tight spaces.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WXvZcoC_yxA

Station 2 — sag|skills

3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg

Station 3 — systems|skills

NZ Give and Go

  • Directions: Objective Develop off-puck movement and teach players to create give-and-go opportunities by moving immediately after a pass. The game encourages players to think ahead, recognize available space, and create new passing lanes to get the puck back. 2 game in the neutral zone .
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcgkBs58qFk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game." Official IHS give-and-go small-area game. Not the NZ-only version; same give-and-go / move-after-the-pass habit.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2jPl1Ind8E0
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hockey Backcheck - Backchecking against a 2 on 1 and 3 on 2." Official IHS backcheck / tracking clip. Not Perry Pearn's 45-degree tracking game; run the written tracking-game rules.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: 2v2 battle off rebound looks. Coach or shooter creates a rebound; both pairs compete for second chances and net-front body position. Excellent goalie tracking volume.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Activation & late D support). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)*) → no-goalie: Neutral Zone Passing Station #1. Partners skate a cone lane making one pass per gap, drop-pass switch at the end, pass back; switch sides every rep. Keeps tonight's focus (Activation & late D support) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM*. Keep Liam's net live and put two tires on the far-end dots — the team attacking that way scores by hitting a tire. Flip ends at the halfway whistle. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *NZ Give and Go* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Pass-to-Score 2v2 / 2v1 Games (one goalie). 2v1/3v2 pass-count game (first to 3 tape-to-tape passes; defender scores on any touch); winners get a 2-on-0 on Liam. Tonight's constraint: the outlet player is a D; the attack only counts once he's activated and touched the puck. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Neutral Zone Passing Station #1; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Perry Pearn Tracking Game* → Play it in Liam's zone; the defending team's controlled exit over the blue line counts as their goal, so no second net is needed. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 v 2 Dot Jumper. 2v2 race on a coach chip; each team's dot player is frozen until it gets a pass, then jumps in for a 3v2 on Liam's net. Theme rule: dot player (a D) must activate below the hash marks before a goal counts. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game* → Run as written on Liam's net, but the coach controls the feed: one shot, play the rebound out, new puck only when Liam is set. Cap at ~12 shots per rotation. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Activated D shoot low for tips; one shot per activation.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey). USA Hockey: warm the goalie first, quality over quantity, and let him hop out for a few reps in high-volume drills.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions

  • Directions: Rondo-style passing progressions (keep-away circles). Start with more attackers than defenders and shrink the outlet time. Cue one-touch options and body shape to receive.

Station 1 — contact|skills

Angle Behind Net + Stick Check

  • Directions: O carries behind the net; X angles to force outside/into the corner and finishes with stick lift/press or controlled rub—no open-ice charge. Switch roles every few reps. Cue: stay slightly behind until the carrier clears the net, then close.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

Station 2 — contact|sag

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Station 3 — sag|skills

The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game

  • Directions: Small-area give-and-go game inside a marked box. Score by connecting give-and-goes or hitting a target rule set by the coach. Cue pass-and-move immediately; sticks on ice for support.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcgkBs58qFk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game." Official IHS give-and-go small-area game. Not the NZ-only version; same give-and-go / move-after-the-pass habit.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position

  • Directions: Skill clip on attack position for 1v1s—hands away, hip protection, attack the defender’s heels/hands. Use as a 30-second demo before 1v1 station work.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lexj0b5n7Ks

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Oreo

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOLeLJdgGA
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "3v3 Continuous." Continuous 3v3 game. Not Lammers' Oreo (D must pass to the next players in line).

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill

  • Directions: Below-the-dots 3v3 rebound battle. Play off goalie rebounds and second chances; defense boxes out, offense crashes with sticks on ice. High-value for Liam’s rebound control.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEFVgm1aC4g
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill." Official IHS net-front / rebound battle. Not Holmstrom's 5-shot box SAG; same screen, tip, and rebound work.

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Middle-ice deny & stick detail). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Angle Behind Net + Stick Check* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*. The race and the 3v3 attack Liam's net; on a change of possession the new team must complete a pass to the coach at the blue line (that's the 'transition') before attacking the same net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net. Below the circle tops, one net; team of 3 must always keep a forward below the goal line, D talk through the switches. Tonight's constraint: defenders get a point for any pass from behind the net they block with a stick. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

Station 3 — contact|sag

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2jPl1Ind8E0
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hockey Backcheck - Backchecking against a 2 on 1 and 3 on 2." Official IHS backcheck / tracking clip. Not Perry Pearn's 45-degree tracking game; run the written tracking-game rules.

C. Small-area game (28–42)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXQlcDUcGKE
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Tursi, "Jets 2v2 drill." IHS 2v2 rush drill on YouTube (Jets 2v2). Not the Pioneer 1v1-to-2v2 progression; same 2v2 rush work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: Two nets back-to-back (or close). Teams attack opposite directions in a tight area, battling for possession and quick shots. High compete, high shot volume for the goalie when one net is live.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k6WXVVGkfTo

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Scoring habits — catch & release). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Angle Behind Net + Stick Check* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3 (*1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*) → no-goalie: Upside-Down Net Target Shooting (no goalie). Lay a spare net on its back against the standing net so only the top strip is open; shoot to the small target. Keeps tonight's focus (Scoring habits — catch & release) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • *Contact sprinkle (Perry Pearn Tracking Game)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 v 2 Dot Jumper. 2v2 race on a coach chip; each team's dot player is frozen until it gets a pass, then jumps in for a 3v2 on Liam's net. Tonight's constraint: the dot player must shoot within one touch of receiving. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Upside-Down Net Target Shooting (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush* → One direction only, into Liam's end; the next pair leaves when Liam is set, and the D come back up the wall as their rest. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Swiss 4 vs 2 Scoring Game. Zone split high/low into two 2v1s on Liam's net (4 v 2); defenders stay in their area, shot within ~5 s. Theme rule: high 2v1 shots must be catch-and-release; low 2v1 finishes rebounds. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game* → Liam covers BOTH back-to-back nets (Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters) format) — or turn one net toward the boards and count only shots that hit a tire set in its mouth. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Catch-and-release from the slot/circles, each off a pass, and Liam sees the passer first — no blind back-to-back shots.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXQlcDUcGKE
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Tursi, "Jets 2v2 drill." IHS 2v2 rush drill on YouTube (Jets 2v2). Not the Pioneer 1v1-to-2v2 progression; same 2v2 rush work.

C. Small-area game (28–42)

The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game

  • Directions: Small-area give-and-go game inside a marked box. Score by connecting give-and-goes or hitting a target rule set by the coach. Cue pass-and-move immediately; sticks on ice for support.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcgkBs58qFk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game." Official IHS give-and-go small-area game. Not the NZ-only version; same give-and-go / move-after-the-pass habit.

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Road Runner 3 v 2

  • Directions: Road Runner 3v2 Overview: Road Runner 3v2 is a high-tempo, continuous rush drill that reinforces key rush principles for both offense and defense. It challenges attackers to make quick decisions off the rush, encourages defenders to manage gaps and sort responsibilities, and teaches the importance of F3 tracking through the neutral zone to kill plays from above. Setup Coach starts with a puck near the top of the circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qGm4xRS8Rkk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Wally Kozak, "Leafs Continuous 3 on 2." Darryl Belfry continuous 3-on-2 rush. Not Road Runner 3v2; same high-tempo continuous 3v2 rush work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey

  • Directions: 3v1 keep-away to train support, deception, and defensive stick positioning. On turnover or after a time limit, flip roles. Progress to 3v2.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6epwQk1POE

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Skating edges, gaps & retrievals). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Side Middle Side* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Liam's station — Station 1: *Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill*. Every rush goes into Liam's end; alternate start corners and send one 2-on-1 every ~20 s so he can set and track the late attacker. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 2: *1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 3: *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Tonight's constraint: coach spots pucks into the corner — first player must win it with a protected retrieval (back to pressure) before a pass. ▶ video

  • *The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Transition Pivot Races; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Road Runner 3 v 2* → Rushes go only into Liam's end; the return rush finishes with a pass through a cone gate at the far blue line instead of a shot. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie). Shot + rebound, then a D-to-D regroup that turns into a 2-on-1 back into Liam's same net (the step-up D must recover his gap). Theme rule: forwards must make the regroup pass on their edges (C-cut, then pass) before the 2-on-1. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey* is goalie-free — run as written; Liam does 2 minutes of easy lateral movement and stretches in the crease.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots come in stride off the retrieval only — no stop-and-blast; one shot max per retrieval rep.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Setup Have a designated forechecker and defenseman on the half wall Set up two gates at the tops of the circles where the defenseman's teammates are The coach (or a player in line) flips a puck into the corner and both players must ska...

  • Directions: 3v1 keep-away to train support, deception, and defensive stick positioning. On turnover or after a time limit, flip roles. Progress to 3v2.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6epwQk1POE

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. The offensive team is trying to skate the puck through the gate while the defender is looking to strip the puck and score on net. Setup Setup a net and a gate as the goals.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xMDs6JiOsBE

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game

  • Directions: Two nets back-to-back (or close). Teams attack opposite directions in a tight area, battling for possession and quick shots. High compete, high shot volume for the goalie when one net is live.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k6WXVVGkfTo

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game

  • Directions: The Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game from Michael Peca was recorded during the 2024-25 NHL Season. This is a high-tempo small-area game designed to develop quick transition skills, offensive movement, and defensive awareness. The drill encourages players to convert defense into offense efficiently while emphasizing strong defensive details and communication.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=526kbcfZPsk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "2v2 Continuous." Continuous 2v2. Not Peca's Sully transition game; same 2v2 transition/compete work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1

  • Directions: The Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1 is an excellent small area game for all age levels that helps players practice a 2 vs 1 in a small space along the boards in the corner of the ice. The game reinforces important skills like keeping your head up, moving to open spaces, protecting the puck, and verbal & non-verbal communication. Offensive players should practice using the boards to make bank passes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnLu_shT2J0

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (NZ transition & play-fast habits). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull the far-end net to the boards and set two tires on the goal line (tire targets). If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Use The Net)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets). Cross-ice; one team shoots on Liam, the other scores by hitting 2 tires at the far end; flip ends every time the tire team scores. Tonight's constraint: play-fast rule — no more than 2 touches per player before passing or shooting. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game*? Liam covers BOTH back-to-back nets (Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters) format) — or turn one net toward the boards and count only shots that hit a tire set in its mouth.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Gates Passing Small Area Game (partners); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game* → One net: on a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the blue line (regroup) before attacking the same net. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Theme rule: defenders' exit pass must be within 3 s of gaining possession. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1* → Already low-volume on one net — keep it on Liam's net and finish each rep with one shot only. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Rush shots need a lateral move or delay first (pre-shot movement) and no more than one rush every ~20 s.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey). USA Hockey: warm the goalie first, quality over quantity, and let him hop out for a few reps in high-volume drills.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

JJHC Varsity Practice — February 15, 2027

FieldValue
DateFebruary 15, 2027
Ice8:30 PM–9:30 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeBreakouts & D-zone exits
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires/pads, whistle

ADM split target: ~50% skills / 30% hockey sense (SAG) / 20% systems.

Board cue: Concepts over choreography. What are we forcing the opponent to do?

Goalie (Liam): Read the system look (breakout rim, PP seam, PK shot lane). Talk early.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–8A. Warm-up + puck flowSkills
8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Directions: Warm-up flow that links retrievals to first-pass exits. Skaters retrieve, hit a support target, and transition up ice without standing still. Great for D breakout habits.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — sag|skills

Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game

  • Directions: 3v3 version of Gates of Buffalo. Teams score by completing passes through cone/tire gates while moving to open ice. Progress by shrinking gates or adding a defender.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adueXqyfyNs

Station 2 — sag|systems

Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

Station 3 — contact|skills

Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUwNEdJtFAs
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "NHL Development Camp Race to Puck Game." Official IHS race-to-puck clip (Sabres camp 1v1 into a 2v1), not Elle Hartje's circle possession game. Same first action: win the puck race.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!

  • Directions: Open practice with a 12-player SAG so everyone is active immediately. Use a half-zone or below-dots box, short shifts, and a simple scoring rule. Sets tempo and compete early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)

  • Directions: Picket Fences is a great small area hockey game that can be setup as a 2 vs. The offensive team gets 2 points for scoring a goal and the defensive team gets 1 point by skating the puck between the tires . Setup: Teams are set up in one of the offensive zones in line with Dots.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sazqSJGB_Ek

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 2 (*Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game*) → no-goalie: Neutral Zone Passing Station #1. Partners skate a cone lane making one pass per gap, drop-pass switch at the end, pass back; switch sides every rep. Keeps tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Puck Race to Possession Game*. Race in the circle; on the second whistle the winner attacks Liam and the loser defends — the defender scores by carrying it out through a blue-line gate. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U))*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Tonight's constraint: defenders need two passes before exiting; forwards forecheck 2-1. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!*? Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free The Gate Game (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp* → One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Theme rule: the below-goal-line rule = breakout start; first pass up the strong side wall. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)* → Already a one-net game (offense shoots on Liam; defense scores by skating the puck between the tires) — run it exactly as written. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Count Liam's rim stops and puck-sets as reps; shots only at the end of an entry, never rapid-fire.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Station 3 — skills|goalie

  • Directions: Offensive-zone timing drill: receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release, weight transfer, and getting the puck through from tough angles. Feed Liam quality looks.

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.

C. Small-area game (28–42)

3 on 3 Add a D

  • Directions: This small-area game emphasizes encouraging your defense to join the rush while working on quick transitions, support, puck movement, and recognizing when to activate the extra player. D. Systems / team (42–54)

2 v 3 Entry Offense vs. Breakout Transition

  • Directions: Objective Develop quick transition habits from defense to offense, with an emphasis on getting two players to the puck quickly and turning possession into an immediate breakout. The game also creates opportunities to work on re-entry rush offense as players transition between offensive and defensive roles. 2 rush with an additional backchecking player, creating a 2 vs.

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
